letters.desc: Constellation supports extending the option to build interconnection facilities to large load customers on the same terms currently available to generator interconnection customers under Order No. 845, giving customers more control over schedule and cost.
quotes: Constellation agrees that the option to build should be provided to large load customers subject to host utility standards as it is currently provided to generator interconnection customers.

letters.desc: Constellation supports giving large load interconnection customers the same option to build interconnection facilities that generator customers received under Order No. 845, arguing customer construction reduces cost and delay and that utility reliability objections were already addressed when that order was adopted.
quotes: Constellation supports extending the option to build to large-load interconnection customers on terms equivalent to those afforded to generator interconnection customers under Order No. 845. Providing qualified customers the ability to construct interconnection facilities under host-utility standards reduces delay, increases certainty, and mirrors the efficiency benefits the Commission recognized when adopting the generator option to build.

letters.desc: Eolian supports extending the generator option to build to large load and hybrid interconnection customers, with clear standards covering all interconnection facilities and stand-alone network upgrades. It warns against utility-discretion requirements that would make the option a practical nullity.
quotes: the Commission should be clear that the developer option to build applies to all interconnection facilities and stand-alone network upgrades, and require facilities to be built to standards and adhere to applicable NERC requirements.

letters.desc: Longroad supports preserving the option for large load developers to construct stand-alone connection facilities, citing national security and consumer fairness when transmission owner timelines or costs are prohibitive.
quotes: National security interests cannot be held hostage to public utility transmission provider delays. If large load can build the "stand-alone" connection facilities faster and at a lower cost than the interconnecting utility, the national security need and fairness to the consumer dictate that it must be allowed.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy opposes extending the option to build to load customers, calling it a failed mechanism even for generators. Data center customers lack NERC compliance obligations, permitting expertise, and utility-standard construction capability, leaving transmission owners liable for facilities they did not build.
quotes: FirstEnergy views the option to build for generator interconnection customers as a failed tariff mechanism that has not resulted in meaningful value or savings that were expected by independent power producers.
Implementation and administration of an option to build for large load data center customers will add significant delay and risk to their proposed interconnections.
As end-use customers, large load customers have no obligations to protect or maintain the reliability of the transmission system, including compliance with applicable NERC standards.
Providing load customers an option to build will put the transmission owner in an untenable position whereby it has compliance responsibilities for facilities that it did not engineer or build.

the best way to achieve the ANOPR's goal of timely large load interconnections is to have experienced transmission-owning utilities design and build the transmission facilities needed to interconnect large load customers.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy opposes extending an option-to-build to large load customers because they lack transmission construction expertise, the generator precedent under Order 845 has produced delays and reliability problems, and transmission owners remain liable for reliability regardless of who builds.
quotes: That principle clashes with the ANOPR's "speed to power" aims: it will introduce delays, inefficiencies, and reliability issues.

large load owners may be sophisticated in other technical fields, but they typically have not been involved in construction of transmission facilities and are not in the same position as transmission owners when it comes to knowledge and expertise regarding transmission facilities.

Transmission owners can ensure compliance much more efficiently when they are the ones building facilities in the first place.  It is not just or reasonable to make transmission owners responsible for reliability of network upgrades constructed by others.

letters.desc: The filer opposes any option for large load customers to construct transmission upgrades. Load customers lack the technical qualifications, NERC reliability obligations, and operational expertise that utilities carry. Extending a build option would likely delay rather than accelerate interconnection, divert scarce engineering talent, and introduce reliability risks.
quotes: Large load customers should not have an option to build transmission upgrades.

Large load customers are not electric utilities, and do not possess the expertise and knowledge associated with developing and constructing transmission upgrades. Nor do they have a legal obligation to ensure reliability.

letters.desc: The filer opposes extending the option to build to large load customers. Generator interconnection experience shows the supervision burden eliminates projected savings, and load is not comparable to generation because it is not competing for access to the system.
quotes: experience with generator interconnections, as well as a recognition of the differences between generators and load customers, demonstrates otherwise.
When factoring in these additional requirements, any potential efficiencies or cost savings are rendered de minimis or non-existent.
Load is not competing with generation for access to the system and is therefore not similarly situated to generation.

letters.desc: LPPC opposes extending the generator option-to-build to load, arguing utilities already have a state-supervised obligation to build for retail load and allowing load to construct transmission facilities intrudes on state jurisdiction.
quotes: This is unnecessary, and inconsistent with planning and operation for retail service, of which large load is a component. The impetus in Order No. 2003 for granting interconnecting generators the opportunity to build out the transmission grid lay in concern that utilities may have a business interest in dragging their feet in providing an interconnection. This is not the case with respect to new retail load, where transmission owning utilities have an obligation to plan, build, and operate facilities under state/local oversight.

letters.desc: The MISO Transmission Owners argue that large load owners lack the experience and expertise to construct integrated network transmission facilities and should not be given the option to build that generators currently hold.
quotes: the MISO Transmission Owners oppose extending the option to build to large load owners

letters.desc: The filer argues large load customers lack the technical expertise and NERC registration to build transmission facilities, that the option-to-build rationale from generator orders does not apply to load, and that allowing it would introduce reliability risks and slow interconnections.
quotes: the MISO Transmission Owners agree with stakeholders who oppose extending the option to build to large load owners

large load owners typically have not been involved in construction of transmission facilities and are not in the same position as transmission owners when it comes to knowledge and expertise regarding transmission facilities
allowing large load customers to have an option to build could slow down the objective of interconnecting large load faster

letters.desc: PPL cautions against extending option to build to retail load customers, drawing on utility experience with generator option to build, which required complex contracting and sometimes produced substandard facilities. PPL argues this would increase costs and risks, working against the ANOPR's goals.
quotes: The PPL Companies caution that expanding option to build to retail load customers is likely to increase costs and risks of interconnection, again frustrating, rather than furthering, the Administration's goals.

Utility experience with generator option to build has largely been negative. At best, utilities needed new and complex processes and carefully negotiated contracts regarding site acquisition, environmental permitting, equipment standards, insurance/indemnity, and numerous other provisions to protect themselves and their customers from poor-quality, expensive, and in some cases dangerous, customer-built facilities.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group specifically disagrees with the ANOPR's proposal to extend generator-style build options to large load interconnection customers. Load customers are not public utilities, lack construction expertise, and the proposal would slow rather than accelerate interconnection. Any such right should require transmission owner consent in the affected zone.
quotes: The SPP TO Group disagrees with this proposal and opposes allowing interconnection customers to build network upgrades identified in expedited large load studies except when agreed by the transmission owner in the affected transmission zone.

allowing large transmission customers who seek expedited interconnection to construct the transmission facilities necessary to support their interconnection request conflicts with the core purpose of the ANOPR: i.e., to enable the interconnection of large new loads and hybrid facilities as quickly as feasible to support infrastructure critical to the nation's economy and security.
Large load interconnection customers are not public utilities and lack experience constructing or developing those facilities.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The filer distinguishes large load customers from generator interconnection customers and argues the option-to-build right should not be extended to load customers who lack relevant construction expertise.
quotes: large load interconnection customers are not similarly situated to generator interconnection customers and should not be afforded the same option to build interconnection facilities and stand-alone network upgrades because they lack experience constructing or developing those facilities.
